tagline: Compare multiple lists with advanced diff and set operations
pageDescription: Professional list comparison tool with set operations (union, intersection, difference), fuzzy matching and developer-friendly output formats. Compare up to 10 lists simultaneously with intelligent algorithms for package dependencies, git files, API endpoints and data analysis. Features Venn diagrams, regex matching, duplicate detection and export to JSON, CSV, SQL. Perfect for developers, data analysts and system administrators managing lists, arrays and datasets. No signup or account required — works directly in your browser as a fast alternative to Excel VLOOKUP or Python scripts.

instructions.title: How to use List Compare

steps.title: Enter your lists
steps.description: Paste your first list into the input panel — one item per line. Add a second list in the comparison panel. Items can be text, numbers, URLs, emails, or any line-separated values.

steps.title: Choose a comparison operation
steps.description: Select the set operation: Difference (items only in one list), Intersection (common items between lists), Union (all unique items combined), or Symmetric Difference (items not shared by both lists).

steps.title: Configure matching options
steps.description: Adjust case sensitivity, enable fuzzy matching for approximate comparisons, or use regex patterns to filter items before comparing.

steps.title: Export and use results
steps.description: Copy comparison results to your clipboard, or export as plain text, JSON, or CSV for further analysis in Excel, Python, or your data pipeline.

features: Set operations: union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference
Fuzzy matching for approximate string comparisons
Venn diagram visualization for 2-3 list comparisons
Duplicate detection and removal across lists
Export results to JSON, CSV, or plain text
Identifies items unique to one list (one-sided difference)
Browser-based — no data uploads or server storage
useCases: Compare package.json dependencies between two projects
Find common items between customer lists or datasets
Identify items present in one list but not another
Discover duplicate entries across multiple data sources
Compare git file lists between branches or commits
Validate that two API endpoints return the same items
Identify added or removed items during data migration
Compare user lists, email lists, or product catalogs
proTips: One item per line works best — paste directly from spreadsheets or text editors
Use case-insensitive mode to avoid mismatches due to capitalization differences
Fuzzy matching helps catch near-duplicates like 'John Smith' vs 'John Smith Jr.'
Use the Venn diagram view for a quick visual overview of shared vs unique items
Export to CSV for further analysis in Excel, Google Sheets, or pandas
For email lists, always use case-insensitive mode since email addresses are case-insensitive
troubleshooting: Items not matching: Check if case sensitivity is causing mismatches — try case-insensitive mode
Empty results: Verify both lists have content and are formatted one item per line
Unexpected duplicates in results: Enable deduplication mode to clean input lists before comparing
Large list is slow: The tool handles thousands of items, but very large datasets may take a moment
Export format issues: Use plain text export as a fallback if JSON or CSV output has encoding issues
